scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4618: URGENT!! The Internet Lab has DISAPPEARED for the
whole Office department!! All morning none of the 128.168.0.x machines answer
any of our PCs (we're the 192.168.3.x ones) -- everything else works, it's
just the lab that's gone. The link that carries us over to the lab is
obviously DOWN -- the wire between the routers on that side has died and
nobody has noticed!! Please bring the link to the Internet Lab back up -- we
need their machines TODAY!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The inter-router links are up, RIP is converged,
  and the 128.168.0.0/16 (Internet Lab) prefix is reachable from the Office segment;
  Office hosts reach 128.168.0.x with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a downed WAN/uplink that is not actually down.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office (192.168.3.x) cannot
reach the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x) -- is NOT reproducible: an Office host reaches
128.168.0.x with 0% loss, the inter-router links carrying traffic toward
128.168.0.0/16 are up, ripd is running on router0/router1/router2, and the
128.168.0.0/16 prefix is present in the RIP tables.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the path to the Internet Lab is healthy
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the Office ->
Internet Lab path, finds it working, verifies the inter-router link state and the
128.168.0.0/16 route, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a downed WAN/uplink
to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
No fault found. End-to-end testing shows the Office VLAN (192.168.3.0/24) can reach the Internet Lab (128.168.0.0/24) normally. From office_pc to pc3 (128.168.0.3), reachability is 0% loss with ~1.33 ms RTT. Targeted probes from multiple Office hosts—enquiry, exam_cell, and tpo—to all Internet Lab hosts (pc2–pc5) also returned 0% loss and sub‑2 ms RTT. Additional check from office_pc to pc2 (128.168.0.2) succeeded. The received ICMP TTL=62 indicates two routing hops, consistent with a healthy path via router1 and router2 over the wan_r1_r2 link; if that inter-router link were down, these pings would fail or reroute abnormally.

Mechanism: Because multiple independent Office hosts can reach multiple Internet Lab hosts simultaneously with consistent low latency, L2 segments, L3 routing, and the inter-router link are all operational. There is no evidence of packet loss, asymmetric paths, or instability.

Localization: No device or interface shows fault; the wan_r1_r2 path between router1 and router2 is functioning.

Root cause: The reported outage appears to be a misinterpretation or an issue that has already cleared; the inter-router “wire” is not down.

Corrective fix: No network changes required. Inform users the link is up. If a specific workstation still cannot reach 128.168.0.x, verify its IP/subnet, gateway, and local firewall, and clear ARP/cache or restart the NIC.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly confirms the wan_r1_r2 inter-router link is functioning and multiple Office hosts can reach 128.168.0.x hosts (demonstrating the Internet Lab prefix is reachable from the Office segment).
